summary: Package root that defines the public import surface of mountainash-transport. It eagerly imports only __version__ and CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE and resolves every other public name lazily through a PEP 562 __getattr__ backed by a _LAZY name-to-(module, attribute) table, caching each resolved value in module globals. A TYPE_CHECKING block mirrors the lazy table so type checkers see static re-exports. It also defines the storage() convenience factory that builds a StorageFacade.
key_functions: storage(provider_type=CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE.LOCAL, profile=None, *, auth_profile=None) -> StorageFacade — convenience factory that constructs a StorageFacade for a provider enum
__getattr__(name) -> Any — PEP 562 lazy resolver: imports the owning submodule from _LAZY on first access, caches the value in globals(), raises AttributeError for unknown names
extension_points: Adding a public name requires three coordinated edits: the _LAZY table entry, the TYPE_CHECKING re-export, and __all__ (tests/test_public_api.py and tests/typing/consumer.py guard the result)

Because backends register on first registry lookup rather than at package import, callers can register a custom backend (register_storage_backend) before first lookup and it wins (tests/test_lazy_imports.py::test_caller_registration_before_first_lookup_wins)
lifecycle_notes: import mountainash_transport is light: only __version__, _core.constants and the docstring-only storage subpackage load eagerly; heavy SDKs (boto3, botocore, paramiko, gnupg, s3fs, minio) must not be imported (tests/test_lazy_imports.py)

Names backed by the [http] stack (settings, connections, HTTP engine, StoragePath/infer_pipeline, profile types) import on first attribute access; on a base install that access raises MissingExtraError naming the [http] extra rather than an ImportError at package import

The storage subpackage is imported eagerly as _storage_pkg before the storage() function is defined so the factory, not the subpackage, is the final 'storage' binding even after 'import mountainash_transport.storage.facade' (tests/test_lazy_imports.py::test_storage_factory_survives_submodule_import_order)
LocationPolicy and LocationNotAllowed are not root exports; they are imported from mountainash_transport.location so stdlib-only consumers avoid the lazy surface
documentation_hooks: Public API reference index grouped by area: facade and factory, read modes (RangePolicy, RangedReadProtocol), storage protocols, connections, settings/profiles, data classes, exceptions, transforms, path helpers, HTTP engine and HTTP error hierarchy
Installation and extras page: which root names work on a base install versus needing [http] or a backend extra
Maintainer note: how lazy exports work and the checklist for adding a public name
Quick start (README) using StorageFacade + Gzip from the root

risks: The _LAZY table, TYPE_CHECKING block and __all__ are maintained by hand in three places; a name added to one but not the others either fails at runtime (AttributeError) or is invisible to type checkers
storage() accepts no policy= argument, unlike StorageFacade(...)/from_path/for_local, so callers using the factory cannot apply a LocationPolicy
storage() parameters profile/auth_profile are unannotated while the rest of the package claims full typing (docs/typing.md)
Errors from a lazily imported submodule surface on first attribute access, not at 'import mountainash_transport', which can move failures far from the import site
open_questions: Is storage() intended to remain a first-class public entry point (it is in __all__ and tested) given README and examples use StorageFacade.from_path/for_local exclusively? Should it gain policy= and annotations?
Should LocationPolicy/LocationNotAllowed be exported from the root (lazily) for discoverability, or is the separate stdlib-only import path a deliberate contract?

evidence.detail: __all__ lists the public surface; _LAZY maps each lazy name to its owning submodule; __getattr__ implements PEP 562 resolution
asserts top-level import pulls in no heavy SDKs, lazy exports are identical objects, and storage() survives submodule import order
asserts root importability of facade, protocols, dataclasses, registry, exceptions, transforms and HTTP names
base-install behaviour: local facade round-trip and remote surfaces naming the [http] extra
Quick start and installation sections document root imports and the base vs [http] split
public typing contracts for root exports
